messages:
sam_support: Hey team — customer ACME is hitting intermittent parse failures in JSON-mode (json_mode=array). They send an array of objects where some items are missing the nested required field `customer.id` and occasionally include an extra `temp_meta` key. Sometimes the payload parses fine, other times we return 502 / Invalid JSON. Customer says it correlates with long arrays (>150 items) and when items come in a slightly different order.

sam_support: Repro from customer (redacted):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "gpt-like-100b",
  "json_mode": "array",
  "prompt": "...",
  "items": [
    {"type":"order","customer":{"id":"C123","name":"Alice"}},
    {"type":"order","customer":{"name":"Bob"},"temp_meta": "x"},
    {"type":"order","customer":{"id":"C125","name":"Eve"}}
  ]
}
```
Response: 502 Invalid JSON: "missing required field customer.id in item 2" (customer sees crash ~1/8 requests)

sam_support: Customer tried SDK v0.8.1 and raw curl; both show same intermittent behavior. Asking for triage and a suggested workaround ASAP.

kai_engineer: Thanks Sam — a few quick Qs: (1) can we get the exact full request/response pair for a failing call including headers? (2) is the customer using streaming responses (stream=true) or non-streaming? (3) which region / route are they hitting? Might be a streaming boundary or our streaming-parser expecting full-array boundaries.

sam_support: Pasted the failing response body they captured (obfuscated):
```
{"error":"Invalid JSON","details":"unexpected token at position 10234","server_trace":"parse_array_at:line..."}
```
They confirmed stream=true in their client for high-throughput ingest. Region: us-west-2.

kai_engineer: Ok that explains a lot. When json_mode=array + stream=true we attempt to parse the whole array as one JSON document after the model emits it. If the model emits partial items or inserts extra keys in some items, our strict schema check (we require `customer.id`) fails during final validation. Streaming can also split tokens mid-item which sometimes leaves trailing commas/partial objects until the final chunk — the parser can return a misleading error if chunks are reassembled incorrectly.

kai_engineer: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Ask customer to set stream=false so the SDK waits for the complete array (quick test). 2) If they must stream, switch to json_mode=per_item (emits one complete JSON object per item) or a newline-delimited format. That way each item is validated independently and missing fields can be handled gracefully. 3) As a temporary workaround they can pad missing nested keys (customer.id = null) on the client side before sending.

emily_prod: Is there a risk this is a server-side bug in reassembly? Customer claims identical requests sometimes pass and sometimes fail — could be race/ordering in our reassembly logic for large arrays.

kai_engineer: Good call — I created a short repro that streams a long array and injects occasional extra key names and item-order permutations. On my node env I can reproduce the failure frequency ~1/12 with stream=true and json_mode=array. Repro notes: SDK v0.8.1, curl chunked encoding, model gpt-like-100b, region us-west-2. Code snippet I used:
```
// pseudo-JS streaming generator
for (let i=0;i<200;i++) {
  let item = {type:'order', customer: (i%7===0?{name:'anon'}:{id:`C${i}`, name:`User${i}`})};
  if (i%13===0) item.temp_meta = 'x';
  yield JSON.stringify(item) + (i<199?",":"");
}
```
When streamed we occasionally observe the assembled array has a stray comma or truncated object boundary leading to parse error.

kai_engineer: Action items: I filed an internal bug (ENG-parse-3247) to harden streaming reassembly and make the final JSON validator tolerant to per-item extra keys when a schema is permissive. For customers currently impacted, recommend switching to per_item or turning off stream. I'll put a canary patch to reassembly in staging today.

sam_support: I relayed the suggested immediate mitigation to ACME and they turned off stream — they no longer see failures after ~100 runs. They asked whether this has billing/latency implications.

kai_engineer: Turning off stream will slightly increase tail latency (client waits for whole output) and may increase time-to-first-byte, but it avoids repeated retries and parse failures that cause customer work. Billing impact is negligible compared to repeated failed attempts. For long-term, our fix will allow safe streaming with json_mode=array; ETA for canary deploy: 48 hours.

deploy-bot: Deployed ENG-parse-3247 branch to staging at 2024-10-12T14:02:31Z (canary environment)

emily_prod: Thanks — Sam, please let ACME know the canary and we can offer to onboard them to the canary if they want earlier validation. Also log the request IDs for the failed runs so we can correlate to the fix post-deploy.

sam_support: Will do. Adding request IDs and customer's contact. Marking as high-priority until canary validation complete. :thumbsup:
